meta.title: Amazon Started in a Garage. Bezos Still Runs It Like Day 1.
meta.hook: Amazon started in a garage in 1994. Jeff Bezos still runs the company like it never left.
meta.description: Jeff Bezos founded what became Amazon from a rented house in Bellevue, Washington in 1994, packing books himself with help from his then-wife MacKenzie Scott. His 1997 shareholder letter introduced the 'Day 1' philosophy — a warning against complacency he has repeated in nearly every letter since.

scenes.narration: Amazon started in a garage in nineteen ninety-four. Jeff Bezos still runs the company like it never left.

visual.visual_intent: A suburban garage door at dusk, warm nostalgic light, still

scenes.narration: Bezos founded the company from a rented house in Bellevue, Washington, packing books himself.

visual.visual_intent: Cardboard boxes and books being packed on a table, warm practical light
visual.decision_reason: founding location and early activity, widely reported

scenes.narration: He and his then-wife MacKenzie Scott built shelving out of doors and drove packages to the post office.

visual.visual_intent: A simple desk made from a door on sawhorses, minimal early-startup office feel
visual.decision_reason: widely reported early-Amazon detail (the 'door desk' is well documented, MacKenzie Scott's involvement is confirmed)

scenes.narration: In his first shareholder letter in 1997, Bezos wrote, quote, this is Day 1 for the internet, and for Amazon.

visual.visual_intent: A printed letter document on a desk, close focus, formal warm light
visual.decision_reason: direct quote from Amazon's 1997 shareholder letter, primary source

scenes.narration: He's repeated that phrase in nearly every letter since. Amazon even named a headquarters building 'Day 1.'

visual.visual_intent: A modern glass office building exterior, daylight, wide architectural shot
visual.decision_reason: Amazon's Seattle HQ building named 'Day 1', widely reported

scenes.narration: The idea: the moment a company acts like it has arrived, it starts losing the urgency that built it.

visual.visual_intent: A close-up of a clock ticking, symbolic of urgency, dramatic light

scenes.narration: Bezos' warning has a name for the alternative. He calls it Day 2. Day 2, he's said, is stasis, followed by decline.

visual.visual_intent: A still, empty office desk, dim light, symbolic of stagnation
visual.decision_reason: Bezos' 'Day 2' framing from later shareholder letters, closing payoff
